title: Cocartesian section quasicategories and parameter currying
statement:
Use quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets and cores as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian sections as in [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration], and $\operatorname{coCart}(S)$ as in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Choose a common containing universe, let $S$ be a small quasicategory, and let $q:Q\to S$ be a cocartesian fibration with $Q$ small in that containing universe. Then the simplicial set $L_q=\Gamma_{\mathrm{cocart}}(S,Q)$ of cocartesian sections, including all transformations over $S$, is a quasicategory. For every quasicategory $A$ in that universe, $S\times A\to S$ is a cocartesian fibration, classified by the constant diagram $\Delta_S A$, and currying induces an equivalence of quasicategories
$$\operatorname{Fun}(A,L_q)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{cocart}}_{/S}(S\times A,Q).$$
Here the right side is the full subcategory of the simplicial mapping object over $S$ on cocartesian maps, with arbitrary transformations over $S$. In particular currying induces an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Fun}(A,L_q)^\simeq\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{coCart}(S)}(S\times A,Q).$$
The evaluation map $S\times L_q\to Q$ is cocartesian, and precomposing it by $\mathrm{id}_S\times a$ represents the displayed map for every $a:A\to L_q$. These comparisons are coherent in $A$, in postcomposition by cocartesian maps $Q\to Q'$ over $S$, and in restriction along every functor $v:T\to S$; the latter uses the induced section restriction $L_q\to L_{v^*q}$ and restriction of maps from $S\times A$. In simplicial degree $n$, currying only rearranges the factors in the same map $S\times A\times\Delta^n\to Q$; both restriction and postcomposition commute with these rearrangements and every simplicial operator.

source.place: HTT Remark 3.1.3.1 (marked mapping quasicategories and their cores), Proposition 3.1.3.3, Proposition 3.1.4.1 and Corollary 3.1.4.4 (cocartesian dual), with the cocartesian-section model used in Proposition 3.3.3.1. Kerodon Proposition 7.4.4.1 (05RX) and Corollary 7.4.4.2 (02TK) use the same section category. The parameter currying and its two naturality compatibilities are an agent-formulated foundation from marked mapping objects and the simplicial exponential identity. Read online; WANTED: archived HTT and Kerodon. No matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: Since $q$ is an inner fibration of quasicategories, [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] identifies its horn-cocartesian edges in the sense of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] with the mapping-square cocartesian edges, so $q$ satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport]. Apply that lemma with $K=S$, $\mathcal E=Q$, $\mathcal B=S$, and $p=q$. Postcomposition gives a cocartesian fibration $q_S:\operatorname{Fun}(S,Q)\to\operatorname{Fun}(S,S)$, so its degreewise fibre over the identity section $\operatorname{id}_S$ is an inner-fibration fibre and hence a quasicategory. The full simplicial subset of that fibre on the sections carrying every edge of $S$ to a $q$-cocartesian edge is again a quasicategory: an inner horn in the full subset has an ambient filler, and fullness retains the filler because all its vertices lie in the specified object set. By the section definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration], this full subset is exactly $L_q=\Gamma_{\mathrm{cocart}}(S,Q)$, including its arbitrary transformations over $S$.

source.place: HTT §§3.1.3–3.1.4, cocartesian section mapping quasicategory; fibre argument written using the definition of an inner fibration

proof.text: The projection $S\times A\to S$ is the pullback of $A\to\Delta^0$ along $S\to\Delta^0$; it is an inner fibration because $A$ is a quasicategory (an inner horn in $S\times A$ over a filled simplex of $S$ is filled in the $A$-coordinate), with fibre $A$ at every vertex. Its edge $(f,e)$ over $f:s\to t$ is cocartesian exactly when $e:a\to a'$ is an equivalence in $A$. Indeed right-pinched mapping spaces of a product are degreewise products, so the mapping square of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] for $(f,e)$ and a target $(u,a'')$ is the product of the square for $f$ in $S$ over itself (a homotopy pullback) with the precomposition map $e^*:\operatorname{Map}_A(a',a'')\to\operatorname{Map}_A(a,a'')$ over a point. Taking $u=t$, where $\operatorname{Map}_S(t,t)$ is nonempty, it is a homotopy pullback for all targets exactly when every $e^*$ is a weak equivalence, i.e. when $e$ is an equivalence. Thus $(f,\operatorname{id}_a)$ supplies cocartesian lifts and the projection is a cocartesian fibration, in the horn sense by the same criterion. For the classification apply the base-change clause of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] to $c:S\to\Delta^0$ and the fibration $A\to\Delta^0$: $\operatorname{St}_S(S\times A)\simeq\operatorname{St}_{\Delta^0}(A)\circ c$, and $\operatorname{St}_{\Delta^0}(A)$ is the object $A$ of $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ by the fibre clause. Hence the projection is classified by the constant diagram $\Delta_S A$, including all higher coherences, not only on objects and edges.

source.place: HTT §3.1.3 and the product case of the cocartesian mapping-square criterion

proof.text: For every $n$, the defining simplicial exponential identity gives a bijection between $n$-simplices of $\operatorname{Fun}(A,L_q)$ and maps $h:S\times A\times\Delta^n\to Q$ over $S$ whose restriction at each vertex of $A\times\Delta^n$ is a cocartesian section. A map $g:S\times A\to Q$ over $S$ preserves cocartesian edges exactly when every $g(-,a)$ is a cocartesian section. One direction holds because the edges $(f,\operatorname{id}_a)$ are cocartesian by Step 2. Conversely, a cocartesian edge $(f,e)$, $f:s\to t$, has $e$ an equivalence by Step 2, and the $2$-simplex $(s_1f,s_0e)$ of $S\times A$ has faces $d_2=(f,\operatorname{id}_a)$, $d_0=(\operatorname{id}_t,e)$, $d_1=(f,e)$. Its image under $g$ has $d_2$ a $q$-cocartesian edge and $d_0$ an equivalence (simplicial maps preserve the inverse witnesses), and an equivalence is $q$-cocartesian because both rows of its mapping square in [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] are weak equivalences. By the composition clause of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] the face $d_1=g(f,e)$ is $q$-cocartesian. Applied to each vertex $i$ of $\Delta^n$ with $g=h(-,-,i)$, this shows that $h$ is an $n$-simplex of the full subcategory $\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{cocart}}_{/S}(S\times A,Q)$ exactly when all of its parameterwise restrictions are cocartesian sections. This identifies the displayed bijections in every degree, and the identification commutes with faces and degeneracies because it only permutes the three product factors. Hence currying is an isomorphism, a fortiori an equivalence, of quasicategories $\operatorname{Fun}(A,L_q)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{cocart}}_{/S}(S\times A,Q)$.

source.place: HTT Remark 3.1.3.1 and the simplicial exponential/cocartesian mapping construction; parameter currying is the agent-formulated foundation stated by the item

proof.text: The map $\operatorname{ev}:S\times L_q\to Q$ is the uncurried identity family: it is the vertex corresponding to $\operatorname{id}_{L_q}\in\operatorname{Fun}(L_q,L_q)_0$ under the degree-$0$ bijection of Step 3 with $A=L_q$, which is a quasicategory by Step 1. Since that bijection lands in $\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{cocart}}_{/S}(S\times L_q,Q)$, the evaluation map preserves cocartesian edges; explicitly a cocartesian edge $(f,e)$ is sent to the composite of the section edge $s(f)$, $q$-cocartesian, and the equivalence $e_t$, as in Step 3. For $a:A\to L_q$, the composite $\operatorname{ev}\circ(\operatorname{id}_S\times a)$ sends $(x,y)$ to $a(y)(x)$ in every degree, which is exactly the uncurried map of $a$ in Step 3.

source.place: HTT Proposition 3.3.3.1, evaluation for cocartesian sections; product factorization written explicitly

proof.text: Taking cores of the isomorphism of quasicategories in Step 3 gives an equivalence (indeed an isomorphism) of Kan complexes $\operatorname{Fun}(A,L_q)^\simeq\cong\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{cocart}}_{/S}(S\times A,Q)^\simeq$; the core is the simplicial subset of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. By [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], $\operatorname{coCart}(S)$ is the infinity category with objects the cocartesian fibrations over $S$ and morphisms the functors over $S$ preserving cocartesian arrows, with higher transformations; it is the coherent nerve of the simplicial category whose mapping Kan complexes are the cores $\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{cocart}}_{/S}(X,Y)^\simeq$ (each $\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{cocart}}_{/S}(X,Y)$ is a full subcategory of a fibre of the inner fibration $\operatorname{Fun}(X,Y)\to\operatorname{Fun}(X,S)$, hence a quasicategory, so this simplicial category is locally Kan). The mapping-space comparison of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] then identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{coCart}(S)}(S\times A,Q)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{cocart}}_{/S}(S\times A,Q)^\simeq$, naturally in both variables. Composing yields $\operatorname{Fun}(A,L_q)^\simeq\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{coCart}(S)}(S\times A,Q)$.

source.place: HTT Remark 3.1.3.1 and Proposition 3.1.4.1, marked mapping quasicategories and cores

proof.text: All naturality clauses are the same simplicial identity. A map $A'\to A$ restricts a family $S\times A\times\Delta^n\to Q$ by precomposition, a cocartesian map $g:Q\to Q'$ postcomposes it, and a functor $v:T\to S$ restricts it along $v\times\operatorname{id}_{A\times\Delta^n}$. Each operation preserves the relevant cocartesian sections or edges: precomposition by $A'\to A$ preserves the vertexwise condition of Step 3, $g$ preserves cocartesian edges by hypothesis, and for $v$, an edge of $T\times_SQ$ whose image in $Q$ is $q$-cocartesian is $v^*q$-cocartesian, since a horn $\Lambda_0^n$ in the pullback is filled by pairing a filler in $Q$ over $S$ with the given simplex of $T$ (horn definition in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]); so a cocartesian section restricts to the cocartesian section $(\operatorname{id}_T,s\circ v)$ of $v^*q$, and for every simplicial operator $\theta:[m]\to[n]$ the two orders of operation satisfy $(g\circ h)\circ(\operatorname{id}\times\Delta\theta)=g\circ(h\circ(\operatorname{id}\times\Delta\theta))$ and the analogous equalities for restriction. Thus currying, evaluation, postcomposition and section restriction commute in every degree, giving the asserted coherence in $A$, under postcomposition, and along every $v:T\to S$.

source.place: HTT Proposition 3.1.4.1, naturality of marked mapping objects; simplicial degreewise verification
